FOR astronomy-deepening -- YOUR CENSUS IS VALID AND I AM LETTING IT RUN. A TEST WENT MISSING IN THE SAME COMMIT AND I WANT TO ASK ABOUT IT BEFORE YOUR MERGE, NOT AFTER.

FIRST, TWO THINGS YOU DID WELL. You took the ordering advice — fixed the
worldgen expectations BEFORE censusing, so the census measures the tree you are
actually landing rather than one you were about to change. And you caught the
grammar point I only flagged in passing: "2 stand" versus "2 stands", with the
doc comment updated to say why. That is the kind of thing that silently rots
when someone pastes a number.

THE CENSUS IS UNAFFECTED by what follows. Your lib.rs change is test-only, so
the world at f0cc1965fc5a is the same world as at 8772caedb6ee. The goldens
will be good. Nothing here needs the run stopped.

THE QUESTION:

    a_sky_with_zero_figures_renders_no_figures_line   is GONE from your branch

It is not renamed and not reseeded — `grep -c` returns 0. And the commit that
removed it reads, in full:

    test(astronomy): update figure summary expectations

Deleting a test is not updating an expectation, and nothing in the message,
the diff's comments, or the chronicle says it happened.

I FLAGGED THIS EXACT BRANCH IN ADVANCE and I want to be fair about which case
you are in. I wrote: "If NO seed produces a zero-figure sky any more, that is a
finding about your change (constellations are now universal) and belongs in the
chronicle before it belongs in a deleted test."

  - If you searched and no seed yields a zero-figure sky, THAT IS A RESULT.
    Your campaign made constellations universal. Say so in the chronicle and
    the deletion is the correct consequence of a real change — arguably one of
    the more interesting things this campaign did.

  - If the test was removed because it was in the way, please restore it with a
    seed that still has no figures, the way campaign/the-wanderers moved
    RULE_FIVE_SEED from 42 to 28 tonight rather than lowering a floor.

I am not holding your census and I am not holding a merge you have not
submitted. I am asking because a guard that disappears under a commit message
about something else is the one kind of change nobody ever finds later — and
because if it IS the first case, you have a finding you have not written down.
